doc_verification.detail: Reachability: no doc_preflight.json sidecar exists anywhere in this plugin tree; two live WebFetch attempts to https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/aliases/update-aliases were both blocked by network policy (domain_blocked, not a 404) — the contract's own source_status field records 'reachable' with verified_at 2026-09-02T12:34:08Z at mining time, so PARTIAL not FAIL. Version: URL segment v-1-18-x and the in-repo authoritative mirror docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json both align with target v1.18.0 on major.minor 1.18 — PASS. Content: the authoritative spec shipped in-repo (openapi/openapi-collections.ytt.yaml L112-133 using the shared response() macro from openapi/openapi.lib.yml L1-35, rendered in docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json L1380-1428) declares for this endpoint only '200 successful operation', '4XX error' (ErrorResponse) and 'default error' — it never literally states 'delete_alias of an unknown alias returns 404 or 500'; the assertion's per-case wording is the contract miner's normalization of the generic 4XX family (raw_knowledge.json expected_responses: 200 ok / 404 not found / 500 internal server error), a reading supported by the family's actual disposition (create-on-missing -> 404, rename-unknown -> 404 observed live) but not literal spec prose, and the operation description (openapi.json L11093) covers only atomicity — PARTIAL. Endpoint: registry path 'aliases+update' POST /collections/aliases (structured_contract.json L5650-5655) matches the spec path, the actix route src/actix/api/collections_api.rs L180 #[post("/collections/aliases")], and the observed request semantics — PASS. All evidence is REST-face; the gRPC face routes through the same storage handler, no SDK/REST confusion.

comparative-forensics note: the gRPC face of update_aliases was not probed by any script (no delete-unknown observation exists via gRPC); per source tracing it shares the identical storage path, so no separate face observation is fabricated here — recorded as face unprobed rather than face_unavailable

http_semantics.note: Strictly worse than the nominal category: a request-side-decidable error condition (delete of a dangling/unknown alias, the same decidability class as create-on-missing which yields 404) is returned as HTTP 200 with a FULL SUCCESS payload (result:true, status:ok) — there is not even a business error code; the response is byte-identical to a successful deletion, so the caller cannot distinguish 'deleted' from 'nothing existed'.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: returns 200 ok; 404 on create_alias of a missing collection; 404/500 on delete_alias of an unknown alias

chain_links: contract: qdrant_behavioral_aliases_update_001 present in structured_contract.json L7595-7606 (evidence_tier=explicit); note — the candidates.jsonl dispatch entry carries an empty constraint_id field for this candidate; the anchor is carried instead by the attack text and by the script header (semantic_aliases_update_004.py L6 'constraint_ids: qdrant_behavioral_aliases_update_001') plus meta.json, so the link is recoverable and intact

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST route src/actix/api/collections_api.rs:180 #[post("/collections/aliases")] update_aliases -> dispatcher.submit_collection_meta_op(CollectionMetaOperations::ChangeAliases) -> lib/storage/src/content_manager/toc/collection_meta_ops.rs:82-85 ChangeAliases arm -> :299 update_aliases -> DeleteAlias arm :321-325 alias_lock.remove(&alias_name)? with no existence validation (CreateAlias arm :316-317 DOES validate_collection_exists, producing the observed 404) -> alias_mapping.rs:72 remove -> Ok(None) for absent alias -> Ok(true) propagates -> HTTP 200 {"result":true}. The gRPC face (src/tonic/api/collections_api.rs:124, lib/api/src/grpc/qdrant.rs:2890/3175) dispatches into the same storage update_aliases, so both faces share the disposition. Official REST tests (tests/openapi/test_alias.py) assert create-conflict 409 and delete-of-existing, but never delete-of-unknown — no test pins the observed behavior.

excluded: env: positive control in the same run returned 200 and case1 returned a precise 404 diagnostic ('Not found: Collection `...` doesn't exist!'), proving the server was alive, authorized, and processing alias ops correctly during the violation

concurrency-race: sequential single-request probes; the identical 200 outcome reproduced deterministically across 3 scripts in separate sessions (timestamps ~35 minutes apart) with freshly generated unique alias names

cache-delay / stale-state: the unknown alias names are freshly minted per run (s2au4_/bau47671c910/sau2_ prefixed), never previously created, so no cache or delayed-propagation state can explain a success response
request-parameter-typo: each script's positive control proves the request encoding and auth path work; the unknown name is a deliberate dangling reference, not a typo of an existing alias
mundane_explanation.surviving: by-design idempotent-delete stance cannot be affirmatively excluded (idempotent DELETE is a legitimate REST design philosophy a maintainer could claim), but it has ZERO in-source intent evidence: no comment/docstring near alias_mapping.rs::remove (grep idempot|by design|intentionally|on purpose = 0 hits in alias code), no test asserting delete-unknown->200, and the same file explicitly returns StorageError::not_found for the identical unknown-target condition in rename_alias — bare silent behavior may not be marked by_design_in_source per v3.4 decision 2, so this is recorded as validation_absent with the by-design defense left for the auditor to weigh
